page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a constrained-core configuration with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, it includes 3780 GB of local NVMe storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier across most compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1792.38 and a multi-core score of 15111.56, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 11346.0. In memory-intensive tasks, the system demonstrates a read-only cached small-block memory bandwidth of 1171.61 GB/sec, which drops to 100.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Notably, the server exhibits strong performance in text processing, scoring 2399.0 in Geekbench text processing, placing it in the top 25% tier. Database operations via Passmark score at 8547.62, and Redis SET operations reach 21.05 million operations per second.

The E64-16ds_v6 offers a specialized qualitative cost-efficiency profile. By constraining the active vCPUs to 16 while maintaining the full 512.0 GB memory footprint of a larger 64-vCPU hardware class, it allows organizations to minimize software licensing costs that are billed per core, while still accessing massive memory and local storage resources. However, the tradeoff is a lower aggregate multi-core compute throughput relative to the massive memory capacity, as evidenced by its average-tier multi-core benchmarks. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive, core-licensed workloads such as relational databases, large-scale caching layers, enterprise ERP systems, and in-memory analytics.
